elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term."
clause gives "thirty (30) days' prior written notice", not 60–90 days

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "without penalty or early-termination charge" — no fee mechanic (more favourable to Customer, but not the fallback bargain)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term 90-day Vendor right

offending_extra_words: subject to Customer's termination and reduction rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4
reasons: All four atomic preferred elements are present in the inserted Section 9.4: Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term. The locked preferred level is satisfied.

Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (30 rather than 60–90 days' notice, no capped early-termination fee, no end-of-term Vendor right), but that is irrelevant because the preferred bargain is complete and the deviations are in Customer's favour.

Minimality fails. The Section 2.1 conforming edit rewrites the tail of the sentence (9 words to 17, changed-character ratio 0.675) when simply deleting "without reduction or termination rights" — or a short "except as provided in Section 9.4" — would remove the contradiction. The official minimality gate flags this operation on both expansion and changed-character ratios, and also that a missing-clause remedy should be delivered by insertion only.

Additional non-essential words in the insertion: "in whole or in part" (partial-termination scope not required by the preferred position) and "without penalty or early-termination charge" (duplicative of the pro-rata refund entitlement and not part of the preferred position).

The reference to "reduction rights" in Section 2.1 has no corresponding operative mechanic in the Agreement; it is harmless (it is expressly limited to rights "under this Agreement") but superfluous and should be dropped.

Intent is preserved otherwise: Sections 8.1, 9.1–9.3 and 9.5 are untouched, the take-or-pay volume commitment and its dollar amount remain effective, and Section 9.4 numbering slots correctly between 9.3 and 9.5 with no undefined terms introduced.
